title: Where and when dogs were first domesticated
summary: There is no firm consensus on the timing or location of dog domestication; Central Asia, East Asia, Western Europe and Siberia have all been proposed.
why: The dog partnership is older than farming, yet its birthplace is unknown.

notes.problem: Third theory's idea gave no explanation; replaced with the source's stated basis.

question: Where and when were wolves first turned into dogs?
evidence: Dogs split from modern wolves 20,000–40,000 years ago; earliest undisputed dog about 17,500 years ago; disputed remains to about 36,000.
wouldSettle: Ancient genomes from early dog and wolf remains pinning the source population and date.

theories.name: Siberian origin
theories.idea: Domestication began in Siberia 26,000–19,700 years ago, though no remains have been found yet.

theories.name: East Asian origin
theories.idea: A mitochondrial study places an initial phase about 33,000 years ago in China or Southeast Asia.

theories.name: Western European origin
theories.idea: The oldest undisputed dog remains, such as the 17,500-year-old Erralla dog, come from Western Europe.
